inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E reported net sales, R$m: H1-26 actual 42,613.4 (ITR, flat on H1-25 42,587.6 as +7.2% organic was offset by BRL translation and the Jan-26 Cuba deconsolidation) + H2-26E 46,570 (H2-25 45,654.9 x 1.02). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027: with a 2026-10-03 valuation date and a 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, omitting H2-26 cash (~R$7-8bn, -3%) roughly offsets discounting FY2027 one year when it is 15 months away (+3%); starting at FY2025 would discount every flow ~0.75yr too long AND double-count H1-26 cash already in the June balance sheet.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, 30-Jun-2026: 15,763.665m issued less 310.870m treasury = 15,452.8m basic (Q2-26 ITR shareholder table) + 66m dilutive options/RSUs (FY2025 diluted-minus-basic weighted gap, 15,683.9 - 15,617.5). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks (R$2.5bn Oct-25 program ~95% done) are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat. No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30-Jun-2026 ITR (R$ thousands in filing): cash 16,610.8 + current investment securities 1,735.6 = 18,346.4; interest-bearing loans 2,949.0 LESS lease liabilities 2,586.7 = 362.2 non-lease borrowings. Leases excluded from debt under treatment (B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow statement 'Share-based payment expenses' 454.2 (ABEV_20F_FY2025.txt:8994); no net-share-settlement tax line in Brazil (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). Interest income = income from cash 1,211.3 + debt securities 192.1 (note 11).
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf follows the contract definition (reported FCF 19,859.9 = OCF 24,450.4 - capex 4,590.5, less SBC, less interest income). It is NOT the component FY0: after lease cash (principal 1,152.3 + interest 271.4), the recurring 'cash net of finance costs other than interest' financing outflow (3,103.6) and NCI (485.0) the FY2025 owner FCF attributable was ~R$13.5bn (R$15.1bn ex a -1.6bn working-capital outflow). The component build's FY2027 base flow (~R$16.6bn) is checked against that.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury-share purchases 1,860.8 (financing); H1-2026 a further 2,652.6. Ambev is a funded repurchaser, so the flat count is paid for in cash.
inputs.fx_note: Model runs in BRL; per-share values converted to USD at USD/BRL 5.2223 (Yahoo BRL=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-02T22:10Z), i.e. fx_rate 1/5.2223 = 0.191487 USD per BRL. 1 ADS = 1 common share. Parity check at inputs.price_as_of: the ABEV3.SA B3 close divided by 5.2223 sits within 1.4% of the NYSE ADS close (close-time and FX-print timing), which confirms the rate, its direction and the 1:1 ratio. Spot conversion of a BRL value is correct because the BRL flows are discounted at a BRL rate (Fisher-consistent); refresh_price.py moves the ADS price but not this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: BRL nominal WACC 12.0% (net cash, so WACC = cost of equity). Built in USD then Fisher-converted, per adaptations (a1): US 10y ~4.3% + beta 0.65 x 4.5% mature ERP = 7.2%, + Brazil country-risk ~2.5pp x ~0.7 exposure (Brazil ~70% of EBITDA; Canada/CAC carry none, Argentina more) = ~9.25% USD; x (1.040/1.023) BRL-vs-USD expected inflation = ~11.1% BRL; +~0.9pp because local BRL real rates (NTN-B ~7% real) price a higher regime than the USD build implies. A pure local CAPM (NTN-F ~13% + beta x ERP) gives ~16% and would value the market leader at ~10x FCF, which the B3 has not priced in a decade. Terminal growth 4.5% BRL nominal = ~4% inflation + ~0.5% real (Brazil beer value CAGR 1.7-2.3% real per industry outlook, mature per-capita). In USD terms that is ~9.25% CoE / ~2.8% g. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows; the same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal 1,152.3 + interest on leases 271.4 = 1,423.7 = 1.6% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT; lease liabilities (2,586.7 at 30-Jun-2026) EXCLUDED from total_debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 6,832.1 - ROU 1,263.8 = 5,568.3 = 6.3% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI (FY2025 485.0 = 3.0% of net income; H1-26 205.1) folded into cash_tax_rate_path as ~2.5pp of leakage on EBIT; no NCI deduction in the bridge, and the put options granted on subsidiaries (inside 'other liabilities' 4,653.0) are NOT deducted, since buying out the minority would return its earnings share — charging both would double-count. Calibration: FY2025 component EBIT ~R$20.3bn x (1-22.5%) = R$15.7bn vs attributable net income R$15.5bn.
inputs.finance_leakage_treatment: Ambev runs a persistent ~R$2.7-3.1bn/yr financing outflow 'Cash net of finance costs other than interest' (FY23 2,731.1, FY24 2,680.9, FY25 3,103.6, H1-26 1,174.4): forward points on the dollar COGS hedges (losses on hedging instruments 1,184.4 FY25), taxes on financial transactions 266.6, bank-guarantee/surety premiums for tax litigation 239.0, FX-acquisition costs in Argentina, plus ~0.5bn non-lease interest paid. It is an operating cost of a dollar-linked cost base in a high-rate currency, recurring every year, so the ebitda_margin_path is 'economic' EBITDA = normalized IFRS-16 EBITDA LESS 3.0pp. Interest income on the cash pile is stripped and the cash is in the bridge, so the carry earned on cash is not used to offset it.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF + non-US adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer'). Ambev is a scale-leader brewer/beverage operating company (~55-66% Brazil beer share), not a bank/REIT/holdco; first valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). Adaptations applied: BRL flows / USD quote (fx_note), BRL-built WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI folded into the tax/leakage driver, recurring hedge/financial-transaction costs charged in the margin, interest income stripped with the cash in the bridge. SBC is small (0.5% of revenue) but non-zero, so the house/street band is narrow, not collapsed. Argentina IAS 29: reported LAS revenue is restated for hyperinflation and translated at closing rates, which inflated the 5-yr revenue CAGR (8.6%) relative to the 3-yr (3.4%); growth is set from BRL inflation + volume/premiumization, not extrapolated. Neither the Q3-2025 trough (Brazil beer -7.7%, NAB -8.6%) nor the World-Cup-aided Q2-2026 (+5.0% Brazil beer) is treated as steady state. Not modelled in the bridge: ~R$ tens of billions of 'possible loss' Brazilian tax contingencies (goodwill amortization, foreign-profit taxation, ICMS) — these are a bear-case risk, not a provisioned liability.

equity_bridge.item: Dividends and interest on capital payable
equity_bridge.note: 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (Q2-26 ITR, R$ thousands 4,194,413); includes the R$1.9bn final tranche of the Dec-2025 IOC paid 6-Oct-2026 to holders of record before today. Cash sits in the June balance; current ADS buyers do not receive it.
~R$1.1bn new IOC approved after the balance-sheet date out of H1-26 earnings already in the June cash; record date assumed passed (Aug-2026) so the current price is ex this distribution.
30-Jun-2026 non-current 'Employee benefits' 1,753.95; debt-like and its interest (107.7 FY25) is not in the margin leakage.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: BRL nominal mid-cycle (~4% inflation + ~1% volume/premiumization), between the equity CAGR floor and the IAS-29-inflated revenue CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 3.6% diverges >30% from revenue 8.6% and EPS 6.6%. Equity is suppressed by Ambev distributing ~100% of earnings (FY2025 R$20.5bn dividends/IOC + R$1.9bn buybacks vs R$15.5bn NI) and by translation reserves, so it is not the primary anchor here; revenue 5-yr is inflated by Argentina IAS 29 and 2020-22 BRL depreciation.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 11,708.9, FY2022 11,627.4 (trough: input-cost inflation), FY2025 18,002.3. The owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported because interest income fell from 2,245.5 (FY20) to 1,403.4 (FY25), not because SBC is shrinking; SBC grew 454.2/208.7 = 16.8%/yr over five years, faster than cash flow, but remains only ~0.5% of revenue. FY22-25 3-yr CAGRs start from a margin trough and overstate run-rate.

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Economic margin = normalized EBITDA - 3.0pp finance leakage. 31.0% = ~34.0% normalized FY27 (FY25 33.4% ex the 643.3 exceptional gain; H1-26 +70bp organic) rising to 35.5% normalized by FY31 on premiumization, BEES marketplace margin and cost discipline; still well below FY2019's 39.4%.
base.capex_pct_path_note: Mid-cycle 6.0%: FY24-25 net capex ran 5.0-5.2% (cut back), the 10-yr average is ~8% (2015-23 capacity build); ex-ROU D&A is 6.3%.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: ~20% operating cash tax (FY25 cash tax 4,187.9 less ~0.48bn on stripped interest income, over ~R$20.3bn component EBIT = 18.3%; P&L ETR FY25 17.7%, FY24 23.8%, H1-26 20.6%; IOC deduction keeps it under the 34% statutory) + ~2.5pp NCI leakage.
base.growth_rates_note: BRL reported growth. ~4% IPCA-linked NR/hl + ~1% volume/mix; non-BRL segments (44% of revenue) translate roughly neutral long-run as BRL depreciates by the inflation differential.

scenario_narratives.base: Brazil beer volumes settle at ~+1% a year after the 2025 weather/disposable-income trough and the World-Cup-aided Q2-2026, with NR/hl tracking IPCA; premium and super-premium (Corona/Stella/Original, ~50% of the premium segment) and Balanced Choices keep mixing up while mainstream erodes slowly; NAB stays a mild drag. BEES marketplace and cost discipline lift normalized EBITDA margin ~1.5pp to ~35.5% by FY2031, recovering part but not most of the gap to the ~39% of 2019. Capex runs at a mid-cycle 6% of revenue, IOC keeps the cash tax rate near 20%, and the CADE/Heineken exclusivity dispute ends in a contained remedy.
scenario_narratives.bull: Premiumization plus BEES monetization (marketplace GMV +58-120%, gross margin ~22% and rising) turn Ambev into a share gainer in a recovering Brazilian consumer: 6-7% BRL growth early, normalized margin back to ~37.5% by FY2031 as aluminum and FX headwinds reverse and the S/4HANA programme completes, capex stays near the recent 5.5%, and IOC deductibility survives tax reform. LAS normalizes as Argentina disinflates.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025 volume softness proves partly structural: mainstream beer keeps losing low-teens in the core tier, GLP-1 adoption and health trends cap per-capita consumption, Heineken's renewed CADE complaint produces a tighter cap on point-of-sale exclusivity, and dollar-linked aluminum/malt costs plus BRL weakness compress normalized margin to ~32.5%. Brazil curtails or abolishes IOC deductibility (repeatedly proposed; Law 14,789/2023 already narrowed the base) taking the cash tax rate to ~24% plus NCI leakage, and capex must rise back toward 6.5% to defend distribution. Growth runs at or below BRL inflation.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: Ambev's normalized margin has fallen from ~40% to ~33% over a decade, a single regulator (CADE) and a single tax regime (IOC deductibility, large 'possible' tax contingencies) are live dependencies, and Brazil volume has been weather/consumer-cyclical. Base 50% as the central mid-cycle path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things — margin recovery, BEES monetization, a benign IOC/tax outcome and Brazilian consumer recovery — to go right together.

entry_price.hurdle_note: House 15% hurdle is a USD (quote-currency) return; the flows are BRL, so it is Fisher-converted: 1.15 x (1.040/1.023) - 1 = 16.9%, rounded to 16.7%. Using 15% on BRL flows would ask only ~13% in USD.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ambev is a mature, cash-generative, net-cash consumer franchise whose value is a BRL owner-FCF stream: margins near a mid-cycle level, growth roughly BRL inflation plus a point, almost all of it distributed. The valuation question is not growth but (i) how much of the lost decade of margin comes back, (ii) whether the Brazilian tax shield (IOC) and the exclusivity-backed route to market survive, and (iii) what discount rate a USD holder should apply to BRL flows. The model is run in BRL at a Fisher-consistent BRL WACC and converted to USD at spot, so the ADS value is not a BRL forecast.
key_risks_to_valuation: IOC (interest on capital) deductibility curtailed or abolished — ~3-4pp on the cash tax rate (bear path)
Brazilian tax contingencies classified as 'possible loss' (goodwill amortization, foreign-profit taxation, ICMS) — not in the bridge; an adverse ruling is a direct equity hit
CADE ruling on Heineken's exclusivity complaint eroding on-trade distribution advantage
Mainstream beer volume erosion / GLP-1 demand headwind outpacing premiumization
BRL/USD: USD value per ADS moves one-for-one with the BRL; fx_rate is a spot print and is not refreshed by refresh_price.py
Hedge carry and financial-transaction costs (~3% of revenue, charged in the margin) rise if the BRL-USD rate differential widens
Argentina IAS 29 hyperinflation and capital controls distort LAS reported growth and trap cash

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (ABEV, NYSE) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.10-3.45 USD. FX Yahoo BRL=X; parity vs ABEV3.SA (B3).
data_sources.financials: Ambev 20-F FY2025 (consolidated IFRS statements, notes 11, 12, 14, 23); Q2-2026 ITR (30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, H1-26 income and cash-flow statements, shareholder table); research/ABEV/Reports/ABEV_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, R$ millions) and kpis.
data_sources.qualitative: research/ABEV/Reports/ABEV_Analysis.json (2026-10-03): segment mix, Q3-25 trough and Q2-26 recovery, BEES, CADE dispute, IOC/tax changes, guidance (Brazil Beer cash COGS/hl +4.5-7.5% FY26).

sanity_check_review.checker_result: scripts/sanity_check.py exit 3: 'Implied P/E 3.3x exceeds 2x the 10yr average 1.0x'; 'Implied EV/EBITDA 1.2x exceeds 1.5x the 10yr maximum 0.6x'.
sanity_check_review.diagnosis: Currency artifact, not a valuation error. The checker divides the USD weighted IV (3.14) by BRL EPS (implied P/E 3.3x), and builds its historical price column by multiplying the USD ADS price by the BRL->USD fx_rate (FY2022 'price' 0.52 = ADS ~2.72 x 0.1915), so both sides are mis-denominated and in opposite directions; EV/EBITDA goes negative because BRL net cash is set against a USD-scale market cap. A priority-order fix (mid-cycle FCF / WACC premium / growth cap / exit cap) would haircut a valuation that is not out of line.
sanity_check_review.fix_applied: none -- trip judged a checker currency-conversion bug on a BRL-filer/USD-quote ticker; valuation left unchanged. Checker needs fixing for dual-currency tickers (fx_rate is model->quote per the Drivers contract).

implied_multiples_after_fix.basis: BRL on both sides, SBC-adjusted (diluted EPS 0.9885 less SBC/share 0.029 = 0.9595; EBITDA FY2025 30,149.8 less SBC 454.2), weighted IV R$16.41, equity R$254.6bn, EV R$243.7bn after net cash 17,984 and bridge -7,048

sanity_check_review.historical_pe_brl: ABEV3.SA Q4 closes / SBC-adjusted EPS, FY2016-FY2025: 21.0, 47.7 (FY2017 EPS depressed by tax-amnesty charge, outlier), 22.5, 25.6, 22.2, 20.0, 16.3, 15.3, 13.2, 14.4 -> ex-outlier average ~18.9x, range 13.2-25.6x. Implied 17.1x is below the average and inside the range: no trip on a currency-consistent basis.
